bihar_raw_news.title: "No two opinions on this": Bihar CM on pay scale promise for non-financed education teachers
bihar_raw_news.content: "No two opinions on this": Bihar CM on pay scale promise for non-financed education teachers ANI | Updated: Sep 20, 2026 23:23 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], September 20 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary attended a teachers' felicitation ceremony at Sri Krishna Memorial Hall in Patna on Sunday. Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Choudhary announced that the Bihar government will implement a pay scale for non-financed (finance-free) education workers and teachers. Highlighting state initiatives in education, he mentioned that the government has disbursed Rs 18,000 crore through the Student Credit Card scheme and emphasised the need to strengthen local educational infrastructure. "I will definitely implement the pay scale we have announced. There are no two opinions on this. I will discuss it with everyone because there are many challenges. Our officer has started working on it. We have formed a committee, headed by the Chief Secretary. I was recently in Delhi. I see how much money is going out of Bihar . We send Rs 18,000 crore rupees through student credit cards. The government pays this. Lakhs and crores of rupees of the common people of Bihar are going out of Bihar for education. We have to improve the infrastructure here. We received a report that most of the students in Kota were from Bihar , and not only the students but also the teachers were from Bihar . We said we had to bring everyone back and started arrangements to bring them back," said CM Choudhary. He further declared that 700 model schools have been established, currently catering to 3.5 lakh children, adding that nearly 1.42 lakh students are also being taught through the Vidyarthi Saathi app. "People said that such a system wouldn't be possible. I proudly say today, go and see our model schools. We started live classes. We're providing JEE and NEET preparation there. Our children will not go out, and we have made arrangements for how a poor child can study at home. You will be happy to know that 350,000 children are studying in model schools, and when 350,000 children need a teacher at 1 a.m., we are currently teaching 142,000 children through the Vidyarthi Saathi app," said CM Choudhary. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: 25 schemes of Modi govt adorns 25 sports cars; Car rally reaches Kashi from Patna marking ...
bihar_raw_news.content: 25 schemes of Modi govt adorns 25 sports cars; Car rally reaches Kashi from Patna marking the completion of 25 years of public service ANI | Updated: Sep 20, 2026 21:11 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh) [ India ], September 20 (ANI): A car rally was organised from Patna to Kashi to mark the completion of 25 years of public service by Prime Minister Narendra Modi as Chief Minister and Prime Minister. Named after Jan Sangh founder Shyama Prasad Mukherjee, the rally included 25 sports cars. Each car was decorated with posters, stickers, and slogans of a central government welfare scheme. The rally concluded at the Village Resort in Babatpur, where winners in various categories were honoured. Car rally coordinator and Bihar BJP Vice President Amrita Bhushan Rathore stated that the rally was organised as part of the ongoing "Seva Sankalp Abhiyan" (Service Resolution Campaign) to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday. She explained that Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary flagged off the rally from Patna. She stated that each car showcased a scheme of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Schemes related to women, health, agriculture, and the welfare of the poor were showcased through separate cars. She added that each car provided information about the central government's development work. Noting that the journey from Patna to Varanasi took four to five hours due to road widening, flyovers, and ring roads, she said that the rally participants praised the Prime Minister's development work. She also reported visiting the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and praying for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's long life and good health. District Panchayat President Poonam Maurya said that the 25 cars that arrived in Kashi from Patna represent Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 25 years of service. She said that Narendra Modi served as Chief Minister for 13 years and Prime Minister for 12 years. During his tenure, efforts were made to transform people's lives through various schemes, including promoting women, empowering daughters, and lifting poor families above the poverty line. District President Ramskal Patel said that Kashi MP and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 25 years of public service will be completed on October 7. He said that during these 25 years, public welfare schemes have benefited the poor and needy, and the country is rapidly progressing in various sectors. At the closing ceremony, the winners of the car rally were honoured with angavastram and mementoes. In addition to first, second, and third place, prizes were also awarded to winners in various categories, including Best Car Decorated, Best Couple, Best Driver, and Youngest Driver. Cars decorated with schemes, Posters, stickers, and slogans representing the Central Government's public welfare schemes were displayed on the cars participating in the rally. Prominent among these were the Ayushman Yojana, the Free Housing and Toilet Scheme, Jan Dhan accounts, the Pension Scheme, the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi Scheme, the Ujjwala Scheme, and the Lakhpati Didi Scheme. bihar_raw_news.title: From Bihar to Punjab: How ChatGPT led elderly man home - The Siasat Daily
bihar_raw_news.content: ChatGPT interface on a computer screen. Photo: Emiliano Vittoriosi/Unsplash A four-day search across state lines ended in an unexpected reunion after an elderly Punjab pilgrim, who disappeared while on a state-sponsored trip to Amritsar, turned up hundreds of kilometres away in Bihar, where a stranger sheltered him and tracked down his family with the help of online searches, reports said on Sunday, September 20. Under the Punjab government’s Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra scheme, Chaman Lal of Fatehgarh Gujran village in Ludhiana travelled to Amritsar on September 11 to visit the Golden Temple. However, he got separated from the group and wandered to Amritsar railway station, his family said. The elderly man has struggled with memory-related issues. From there, it turns out, Lal boarded a train heading to Bihar and travelled to Gaya, more than 1,200 kilometres from home. In Gaya, Neeraj noticed Lal wandering and asking for food. According to Neeraj, while Lal could not recall his address, “He could only remember the name of his village, Fatehgarh Gujran.” Speaking to The Statesman , Neeraj said he took Lal home to stay while he tried to find the elderly man’s village. Three days of research on ChatGPT Since Lal was speaking Punjabi, that helped Neeraj narrow down his search to that state. He used ChatGPT and other internet searches to identify Fatehgarh Gujran as a village near Machhiwara Sahib in Ludhiana. A three-day search was all it took. Neeraj then accompanied Lal from Gaya to Ludhiana and then to Machhiwara, where he showed his photograph to locals on Saturday. Local man Master Krishan Lal recognised Lal from a missing-person photograph circulated on social media and contacted his grandson, Sukhchain Singh. Singh then reached Machhiwara and was reunited with his grandfather. “We searched for him in Amritsar but could not find him. I am extremely thankful to Neeraj for keeping my grandfather safe and bringing him back,” Singh was quoted as saying. Meanwhile, for Neeraj, this isn’t new; the construction sector employee in Gaya has been helping people in distress since his school days. “When I saw him alone at the station, I felt I should help him,” he said. bihar_raw_news.title: CM Samrat Chaudhory calls for everyone's participation in building a prosperous Bihar
bihar_raw_news.content: CM Samrat Chaudhory calls for everyone's participation in building a prosperous Bihar ANI | Updated: Sep 20, 2026 19:43 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [ India ], September 20 (ANI): Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhory inaugurated the 'Viksit Bihar : Foundation to Construction' (Viksit Bihar : Neev se Nirman tak) brainstorming session and 'Lav-Kush Pratibha Samman Samaroh' (Talent Felicitation Ceremony) by lighting the ceremonial lamp at the Bapu Sabhagar within the Samrat Ashok Convention Centre. Talented individuals who excelled in various fields were honoured at the event, which was organised by the Progressive Intellectuals Association, Bihar . According to the Chief Minister's Office, the Chief Minister stated that the foundation of unity for the Lav-Kush community was laid in 1994, and this unity remains intact today. He emphasised that the Lav-Kush community is not against anyone; rather, it seeks to play its role in the prosperity of Bihar and the development of the nation while moving forward with a commitment to justice. Following the 'Kurmi Chetna Rally' and 'Kushwaha Sammelan' in 1992-93, both communities jointly organised the 'Lav-Kush Sammelan' in 1994. He extended his congratulations to all the leaders who initiated this movement. He noted that this social unity subsequently took on a political form and played a crucial role in advancing the political parties associated with it. “Today is the time to realise the vision of a developed India and a prosperous Bihar . Prime Minister Narendra Modi has envisioned a developed India , while former Chief Minister of Bihar Nitish Kumar has envisioned a prosperous Bihar ; we are working to turn these visions into reality,” he said. The Chief Minister remarked that Bihar possesses a glorious history. Great rulers like Chandragupta Maurya and Emperor Ashoka provided direction to India and the world from this very land. There is a need to present Bihar 's historical and cultural heritage to the world with greater emphasis. He noted that significant changes have occurred in Bihar 's economy and infrastructure since 2005. At the time of the bifurcation of Bihar and Jharkhand, Bihar 's economy was largely dependent on revenue generated from Jharkhand; however, today, Bihar 's budget has far surpassed that of Jharkhand. He noted that in 2024, while Jharkhand presented a budget of Rs 1.39 lakh crore, Bihar presented a budget of Rs 3.17 lakh crore. The Chief Minister stated that academic sessions commenced simultaneously in 211 degree colleges across Bihar on July 15. Additionally, 700 model schools (Saraswati Vidya Niketan) have been established, catering to 3.5 lakh students. bihar_raw_news.title: Ishan Anand to get 'respectable role' in BSP, Mayawati rules out Akash's return
bihar_raw_news.content: September 20, 2026 Ishan Anand to get 'respectable role' in BSP, Mayawati rules out Akash's return Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service BSP supremo Mayawati on Sunday said her younger brother Anand Kumar's son Ishan Anand would be given a "respectable role" in the party, while ruling out any change in her decision to keep his siblings Akash Anand and Deepika away from organisational responsibilities. The announcement comes about a week after Mayawati had said that neither of Anand Kumar's sons, Akash and Ishan, would be allowed to hold any post in the Bahujan Samaj Party, amid an ongoing family dispute that has seen repeated changes in the political roles of her relatives. In a post on X, Mayawati said Akash, the party's former chief national coordinator, and Deepika would be kept "completely away" from any responsibility in the BSP. "In the interest of the party, it would be appropriate to keep Akash Anand and his sister (Deepika) completely away from giving any responsibility in the party. There will be no change in this decision," she said. "Now, in place of both of them, only Ishan Anand from Anand Kumar's family will be given a respectable role in the party and taken forward," she added. Mayawati warned that Ishan too would face expulsion if he committed any "serious anti-party act". In that event, she said, no other member of Anand Kumar's family would be given any responsibility, big or small, in the party. On Akash, Mayawati said his conduct and activities after marriage had led to his being separated from the party again. She also alleged that Akash was "completely caught in the web" of his father-in-law Ashok Siddharth and said bringing him back into the party would amount to a "very big betrayal" of the BSP. Mayawati said she had been in a dilemma over whom from Anand Kumar's family should be given a role in the party and had taken the latest decision after considering the issue from "every aspect". She also said she had decided against seeking Deepika's help in future after her marriage, expressing concern that her case could turn out to be similar to Akash's. On September 12, Mayawati had described her decision as her "final decision and pledge", saying neither Akash nor Ishan would be given any political post in the BSP. At the time, she had said Anand Kumar could seek assistance from his daughter Deepika, who is studying law. Mayawati also invoked BSP founder Kanshi Ram, saying he had kept his close relatives away from political benefits after entering politics and that she too had decided to follow his example. On September 10, Mayawati had announced that Akash, who is married to a daughter of former Rajya Sabha member Ashok Siddharth, had been completely relieved of his responsibilities in the BSP. She had earlier removed Siddharth from the party. Mayawati's younger brother Anand Kumar is the BSP's national vice-president. She had first appointed him to the post in 2017

bihar_raw_news.title: Jan Suraaj announces candidates for 5 Bihar Legislative Council seats
bihar_raw_news.content: Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor Prashant Kishor-led Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) on Sunday announced candidates for five Bihar Legislative Council constituencies, getting an early start on elections to eight graduates’ and teachers’ seats that are expected to be announced soon. The terms of members representing the eight constituencies — four graduates’ and four teachers’ seats — are due to expire in November. Jan Suraaj has already said it plans to contest all eight seats as part of its organisational expansion in Bihar. Announcing the candidates at a press conference, Kishor said Afaq Ahmed would seek re-election from the Saran teachers’ constituency. Ahmed had won the seat six years ago with Kishor’s support, before the former poll strategist launched Jan Suraaj as a political party. Divya Jyoti, a lawyer and academician-turned-politician who joined Jan Suraaj last week, will contest from the Patna teachers’ constituency. The seat is currently held by JD(U) chief spokesperson Neeraj Kumar. The party has named S P Rai as its candidate from the Darbhanga teachers’ constituency, while Ravindra Yadav will contest the Darbhanga graduates’ seat. Rajnish Ranjan has been fielded from the Kosi graduates’ constituency. Live Events The Legislative Council election is separate from the Bihar Assembly polls and will cover graduates’ and teachers’ constituencies spread across around 30 districts of the state. Unlike Assembly elections, the contests are decided by specialised electorates comprising eligible graduates and teachers. Candidates’ local influence, their standing among these voters and the organisational strength of their parties are expected to play an important role in the eight contests. With five candidates now declared, Jan Suraaj has three more nominees to announce if it goes ahead with its plan to contest all eight seats. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! bihar_raw_news.title: Lost in Amritsar, found in Bihar : Stranger uses ChatGPT to reunite elderly Punjab man with family
bihar_raw_news.content: Pic courtesy: SNS Subscribe to Notifications An elderly Punjab man who went missing during a government-sponsored pilgrimage to Amritsar was reunited with his family after travelling by train to Bihar, where a stranger sheltered him for four days and used internet searches to trace his village, his family said. Chaman Lal, a resident of Fatehgarh Gujran village in Ludhiana district, had travelled to Amritsar on Sept. 11 under the Punjab government’s Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra scheme to visit the Golden Temple. Lal, who has memory problems, became separated from other members of the group and wandered towards Amritsar railway station, according to his family. He then boarded a train bound for Bihar and eventually reached Gaya, they said. His grandson, Sukhchain Singh, travelled to Amritsar after being informed that Lal was missing and lodged a complaint with police. Family members and villagers also circulated Lal’s photograph on social media as the search continued. In Gaya, a local resident identified as Neeraj said he noticed Lal wandering near the railway station and asking for food. “He could not tell me his address. He could only remember the name of his village, Fatehgarh Gujran,” Neeraj said. Neeraj said he took Lal home, gave him food and allowed him to stay with his family while he tried to establish where the village was located. Lal spoke Punjabi, which led Neeraj to focus his search on Punjab. He said he used ChatGPT and other internet searches over several days before identifying Fatehgarh Gujran as a village near Machhiwara Sahib in Ludhiana district. “I kept searching for about three days. Once I found that the village was near Machhiwara, I decided to take him back myself,” Neeraj said. Neeraj travelled with Lal from Gaya to Ludhiana and then to Machhiwara, where he showed the elderly man’s photograph to local residents on Saturday. A local resident, Master Krishan Lal, recognised Lal from a missing-person photograph that had been circulated on social media and contacted his grandson. Sukhchain Singh then reached Machhiwara and was reunited with his grandfather. “We searched for him in Amritsar but could not find him. I am extremely thankful to Neeraj for keeping my grandfather safe and bringing him back,” Singh said. Neeraj said he works in the construction sector in Gaya and has been helping people in distress since his school days. “When I saw him alone at the station, I felt I should help him,” he said. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Demand for 'Marcha Chuda' soars after GI tag ; unique aroma becomes its trademark
bihar_raw_news.content: Home News National News Bihar: Demand for ‘Marcha Chuda’ soars after GI tag; unique aroma becomes its trademark In Short Because of the high demand for the aromatic ‘Marcha Chuda’, it is being exported to multiple Indian cities and abroad, increasing demand for cultivation in Champaran's local farmlands. IANS Created On: 20 Sept 2026 8:54 PM IST Comment Share : X Demand for the aromatic ‘Marcha Chuda’ A− Font size A+ Select Hans India Now FOLLOW ON G o o g l e News Patna: Demand for the aromatic ‘Marcha Chuda’ (flattened rice from West Champaran) has soared both domestically and internationally after the famous food item earned the official GI (Geographical Indication) tag. Because of the high demand for the aromatic ‘Marcha Chuda’, it is being exported to multiple Indian cities and abroad, increasing demand for cultivation in Champaran's local farmlands. A group of Marcha Chuda cultivators speaking to IANS shared that rising demand for their produce has accelerated cultivation and production. One of the most distinctive features of Marcha Chuda is its unique aroma, which fills their homes and the village with its fragrance. He explained that the GI tag has helped people understand Marcha Chuda’s significance and unique qualities. Ramji Prasad said the specific characteristic derived from Champaran soil distinguishes Marcha Chuda from varieties grown elsewhere. Sharing details of rising income due to increased Marcha Chuda cultivation, he said farmers in certain areas of Champaran are cultivating it and reaping economic benefits. He also urged fellow farmers to increase production, as it helps both farmers and traders capitalise on the rising demand. Marcha Chuda sells for approximately ₹150 per kilogram. Higher demand for the crop means extra income for those involved in its cultivation. Cultivation of Marcha paddy usually begins during the month of Sawan, and the crop is ready for harvest by the end of November. Unlike Marcha Chuda from other regions, Champaran's has a special impact because of its aroma. Farmers cultivate it using traditional, organic methods, without chemicals or fertilisers. The unique shape of Marcha Chuda also sets it apart from other varieties. Its grain resembles a black peppercorn, which is why it is known as 'Marcha' or 'Marcha paddy'. This is currently being transported to states like Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Odisha, Uttarakhand, and Jharkhand. According to Ramji Prasad, his family has been in the Marcha Chuda business since 1969. Initially, this was done entirely by hand—a labour-intensive and time-consuming task — but in 1997, machinery entered the process. Over time, various innovations followed, making flattened rice cultivation easier and faster. Approximately 50 to 60 quintals of Marcha Chuda are produced every month in his village, employing around 100 people. bihar_raw_news.content: SIGN IN Edition IN IN US Download App Follow Us On: News India Today Insight Why Bihar is investing big infra in Gaya’s sacred geography Get 37% off on an annual Print + Digital subscription of India Today Magazine SUBSCRIBE Why Bihar is investing big infra in Gaya's sacred geography The revamp of the Vishnupad Temple precinct along Kashi Vishwanath Corridor lines and Son-Falgu river-linking, costing Rs 3,516 crore, aim for a durable pilgrimage economy Advertisement Amitabh Srivastava UPDATED: Sep 20, 2026 16:57 IST Edited By: Ashish Mukherjee Bihar’s Samrat Choudhary government, on September 15, put Gaya on the fast track to development, approving a Rs 3,516 crore package that brings together two seemingly unrelated projects. One is the Rs 2,520 crore redevelopment of the Vishnupad Temple precinct on the lines of Varanasi’s Kashi Vishwanath Corridor. The other is a Rs 996.05 crore project to link the Son and Falgu rivers. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Taken together, the two projects point to a larger ambition: if Gayaji is already one of Bihar’s biggest religious-tourism destinations, its infrastructure must keep pace with the scale of its pilgrimage economy. That means not only upgrading the spaces around its sacred sites but also addressing the water challenge that has long shaped the Falgu. The September 15 cabinet approval is part of Choudhary’s broader push to develop Bihar’s religious-tourism centres and give them infrastructure commensurate with their growing significance. Gaya is one of the few places in the state that draw a great number of Indian pilgrims and foreign visitors. Provisional Bihar tourism figures for January to July 2026 put domestic tourist visits to Gaya at 1.14 million; alongside are 96,465 foreign visitors. This is in addition to the footfalls recorded at Bodh Gaya, where another 1.46 million domestic visitors and 134,000 foreign visitors were recorded in the same period. Together, the two destinations accounted for about 231,000 foreign visitors in the first seven months of the year. The scale becomes more striking when placed against the state capital. Patna recorded only 6,429 foreign visitors in the same seven-month period, according to the provisional figures. In other words, the Gaya-Bodh Gaya belt is the state’s principal meeting point between two very different streams of religious travel—Hindu pilgrimage at Gaya and global Buddhist pilgrimage at Bodh Gaya. And even those numbers understate the annual load. The January-July figures do not capture the Pitripaksha Mela, which falls in September-October. That is when Vishnupad, the Falgu ghats and the city’s pind daan economy get their biggest annual rush. The government's Vishnupad plan reads almost like a response to that pressure: multi-level parking, elevated pathways, ghats, bridges, ramps, dormitories, a canteen, pedestrian infrastructure and public amenities are all part of the package. The project will be implemented by the Bihar State Road Development Corporation. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Govt Hospitals directed to ensure 100 per cent digital OPD registration
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Govt Hospitals directed to ensure 100 per cent digital OPD registration Written By : Medical Dialogues Team Published On 2026-09-20T16:15:42+05:30 | Updated On 20 Sept 2026 4:16 PM IST Patna: Government hospitals across Bihar have been directed by the state Health Department to ensure 100 per cent digital registration of patients in outpatient departments (OPDs), as part of efforts to strengthen digital health records and expand online healthcare services. The directions were issued during a review meeting chaired by Health Secretary Kumar Ravi on Wednesday. Hospitals have been asked to use ABHA-based registration and electronic health records (EHRs) for patients , while also expanding online consultation services and regularly monitoring doctors ’ digital attendance. For patients admitted to inpatient departments, registration through the Bhavya portal has also been made mandatory. The department has asked officials to closely monitor implementation of these digital systems at healthcare facilities. The review meeting also focused on the referral of patients from government hospitals. Officials were directed to prevent avoidable referrals and ensure that patients are shifted to higher centres when specialised treatment or facilities are genuinely required. Also Read:Amit Shah to inaugurate New KLE Medical College Building, 1,200-bed Hospital in Hubballi Maternal and child healthcare was another focus area, with the department directing officials to strengthen efforts to prevent deaths and take action where negligence is found. The selection of ASHA workers was also reviewed, with instructions to ensure recruitment remains within the prescribed targets. The department further assessed plans to upgrade district hospitals into super-speciality medical centres and develop community health centres as specialised treatment facilities. Progress under the TB-Free Bihar and Anaemia-Free Bihar campaigns was also reviewed. The review also covered surgical services at district hospitals. Data presented during the meeting showed that 2,428 surgeries were performed in June 2026, 5,650 in July and 8,209 in August. Under the Ayushman Bharat scheme, the corresponding number of surgery claims was 1,000 in June, 1,331 in July and 1,626 in August, Patna Press reported. Meanwhile, the Health Department has directed officials to complete ongoing repair and improvement work in government hospitals by October 31. The work includes painting, minor repairs, drinking water facilities, toilets, waiting areas and nursing desks. The improvement programme covers 36 district hospitals, 56 sub-divisional hospitals, 49 referral hospitals, 332 community health centres, 110 primary health centres, 147 urban primary health centres, 844 additional primary health centres and Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. The meeting was attended by senior officials from the Bihar Medical Services and Infrastructure Corporation and the State Health Society, among others. national_raw_news.content: Indian Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh and Japan Air Self-Defense Force Chief of Staff General Takehiro Morita flew together in India’s indigenous Light Combat Aircraft Tejas during a formation sortie in Jodhpur today. The flight by the air chiefs of both nations comes as the Indian Air Force and Japan Air Self-Defense Force are conducting the joint air exercise ‘Veer Guardian 2026’ in Jodhpur. This is the first time that Japanese fighter aircraft are operating from Indian soil as part of a bilateral exercise, further deepening the defence partnership between both the countries. Talking to media in Jodhpur after the sortie, Air Chief Marshall Singh said, first-ever operation of Japanese fighter jet on Indian soil marks major milestone in bilateral defence ties. The Japanese Air Chief appreciated the warm hospitality extended by the Indian side and described the Tejas as a symbol of India’s technological innovation and the country’s Make in India initiative The 14-day exercise, which will conclude on Tuesday, focuses on advanced operational missions and extensive professional interactions between the two air forces. The exercise involves a diverse mix of Indian Air Force frontline combat aircraft, including the indigenous Light Combat Aircraft Tejas, Su-30MKI and Rafale while Japan is participating with F-2A fighter aircraft.

national_raw_news.title: 56 mins ago | National 29 President Murmu calls for stronger climate action and global cooperation to tackle rising natural...
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has said numerous natural disasters in recent times have made it clear that robust climate action is essential to mitigate climate impacts. Addressing the valedictory session of the conference on the Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics in New Delhi this evening, the President said the global scientific community is warning that climate risk has become very serious. She stressed on the need to strengthen active cooperation among stakeholders at local, regional, and global levels to prevent and address the issue. The President said, climate change is also having serious repercussions on food security, health, and livelihoods. President Murmu said, it is well known that climate change is causing imbalances across various levels of human existence. She said, biodiversity loss, water stress and land degradation are examples of the imbalances. The President said that farm pods can be useful for the local community in the water-stress regions. She said, a well-structured framework of policies and actions is essential to effectively address such a complex challenge. President Murmu said, the framework must ensure the active participation of not only governments and legal experts but also the communities most affected by climate change. She said, special sensitivity towards the needs of rural and forest-dwelling societies, small farmers, women, and other vulnerable communities is crucial, as they bear the brunt of natural disasters. The President underlined that traditional knowledge systems, along with the practices and lived experiences of local communities, play a vital role in enhancing climate adaptation capacity. She stressed on strengthening climate resilience through people-centric and community-based adaptation approaches rooted in traditional knowledge. President Murmu stated that sustainable afforestation can also play a significant role in enhancing climate resilience. She said, afforestation efforts that nurture biodiversity and are aligned with local conditions can be instrumental in this regard. She added that the true objective of sustainable afforestation is not merely planting trees, but rather restoring healthy and self-sustaining ecosystems. The President said that developing countries should chart a path that enhances resilience while maintaining the pace of development. She said, commitments to responsible climate action must align with the country’s development needs and economic aspirations. She added that they must also be technically feasible. The President said that India has done commendable work in fostering environmental awareness by engaging common citizens, especially the youth. She said, the Government of India’s ‘Mission LiFE’ initiative has demonstrated that meaningful strides towards ecological restoration can be achieved through public participation and community ownership. She said, the National Green Tribunal plays a pivotal role in environment-related legal matters. President Murmu said, the Tribunal has expeditiously resolved a vast number of disputes. She said, the tribunal has developed an effective compliance framework regarding rivers, air quality, and waste management in the country. Union Minister for Power, Housing and Urban Development Manohar Lal, Judge in Supreme Court Justice B V Nagaratna, Chairman National Green Tribunal Justice Prakash Shrivastava, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta also addressed the valedictory session of the conference.

national_raw_news.title: Bogibeel IWT Terminal National Waterway-2 Visit Overview - Pragativadi I Latest Odisha ...
national_raw_news.content: Bogibeel IWT Terminal National Waterway-2 Visit Overview - Pragativadi I Latest Odisha News in English I Breaking News About us Privacy Policy Disclaimer Contact Sunday, September 20, 2026 EPAPER Odisha Twin City Politics National World Sports Entertainment Business Lifestyle Tech Quiz Prativa Vikash 2026 No Result View All Result EPAPER Odisha Twin City Politics National World Sports Entertainment Business Lifestyle Tech Quiz Prativa Vikash 2026 No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home » Bogibeel IWT Terminal and NW-2: How Brahmaputra Waterways Can Transform Northeast and Odisha Logistics Bogibeel IWT Terminal and NW-2: How Brahmaputra Waterways Can Transform Northeast and Odisha Logistics Odisha media team reviews Brahmaputra terminals as IWAI maps a river-to-port logistics model for the Northeast and Odisha by Yajati Rout September 20, 2026 in Odisha Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 0 0 21 VIEWS A media delegation from Odisha, led by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) Bhubaneswar, on Sunday began a five-day exposure tour of Assam to study major infrastructure and logistics projects in the Northeast. The first stop was the Bogibeel Inland Water Transport (IWT) Terminal on the Brahmaputra, along with the 4.94-km Bogibeel Bridge — India’s longest combined rail-and-road span across the river. The visit was designed as more than a site inspection. IWAI officials used the terminal to explain how National Waterway-2 (NW-2) is being built as a low-cost cargo, passenger and strategic corridor — and how a similar model is being prepared for Odisha’s National Waterway-5 (NW-5) on the Brahmani–Mahanadi system. What the terminal can do IWAI official Sunil Shinde briefed the visiting journalists on operations at Bogibeel, commissioned as a modern tourist-cum-cargo facility on NW-2. The terminal has berthing infrastructure for vessels up to 1,000 MT (flotilla) and an annual cargo handling capacity of about 6 lakh metric tonnes. Officials said it currently supports multimodal movement of crude oil and petroleum products from the Dibrugarh belt, besides tea, coal, stone aggregates and cement. The waterway is also being used for heavy Over-Dimensional Cargo (ODC) linked to the capacity expansion of the Numaligarh Refinery. The tourist-cum-cargo terminal received its foundation stone from Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal on 4 July 2023. Construction began around June 2023. In February 2026, Customs and Immigration complexes at Bogibeel and Dhubri were inaugurated, tightening the terminal’s role on the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route. A Regional Centre of Excellence and additional cruise facilities are also being developed at Bogibeel. Why the river route matters NW-2 — the 891-km Brahmaputra stretch from the Bangladesh border to Sadiya — was declared a national waterway on 1 September 1988. About 12 terminals are now maintained for cargo vessels, passenger ferries and Ro-Ro services. Key points include Dhubri, Jogighopa (a Port of Call and multimodal hub), Pandu in Guwahati with rail connectivity, Tezpur, Silghat, Biswanath Ghat, Neamati, Bogibeel, Dibrugarh, Sengajan/Panbari and Oriumghat. IWAI maintains navigable depth through regular dredging: 2.5 metres from the Bangladesh border to Neamati, 2.0 metres from Neamati to Dibrugarh/Bogibeel, and 1.5 metres from Dibrugarh to Sadiya....

national_raw_news.title: Union Sports Minister Mandaviya leads Indian diaspora at 'Sundays on Cycle' in Nagoya to ...
national_raw_news.content: Union Sports Minister Mandaviya leads Indian diaspora at 'Sundays on Cycle' in Nagoya to Cheer for Bharat Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Sports Minister Mandaviya leads Indian diaspora at 'Sundays on Cycle' in Nagoya to Cheer for Bharat ANI | Updated: Sep 20, 2026 14:06 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Aichi-Nagoya [Japan], September 20 (ANI): Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports Mansukh Mandaviya led the 91st edition of ‘Sundays on Cycle’ at Meijo Park in Nagoya, Japan, on Sunday, September 20, 2026, where he rallied together members of the Indian diaspora to extend support and encouragement to the Indian contingent participating in the Asian Games 2026. The initiative reflected the Government of India's continued efforts to strengthen people-to-people connect with the Indian diaspora through the universal language of sports, while reinforcing the message of fitness and healthy living under the Fit India Movement, as per a press release from the Union Sports Ministry. Mandaviya interacted with participants of the 91st Sundays on Cycle event and appreciated their enthusiasm for coming together to support Team India in the Asian Games. The Indian community in Nagoya came together through ‘Sundays on Cycle’ to ‘Cheer for Bharat’ and boost the morale of the athletes participating on the biggest continental stage. “The Asian Games have commenced in Nagoya, Japan, and we have a contingent of over 500 young athletes from India, who are participating in the Games,” said Dr Mandaviya. “The Indian diaspora in Nagoya has shown great enthusiasm to support and cheer our athletes by joining the Sundays on Cycle event here,” he said. “I am happy to say that our contingent is performing well, and our diaspora is working hard to boost their morale," he added. Mandaviya is in Nagoya, Japan, for the Asian Games 2026, where he is interacting with Indian athletes, officials, and members of the Indian diaspora, underscoring the Government's sustained efforts towards promoting sports excellence and a fitter, healthier India on the global stage. Fit India Sundays on Cycle is organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) in collaboration with the Cycling Federation of India (CFI), Raahgiri Foundation and MY Bharat. The cycling drive is conducted simultaneously across all States and Union Territories, including at SAI Regional Centres, National Centres of Excellence (NCOEs), SAI Training Centres (STCs), Khelo India State Centres of Excellence (KISCEs) and Khelo India Centres (KICs). Over 6000 NAMO Fit India clubs also organise the cycling initiative nationwide every week. national_raw_news.title: Three-Day IAF Air Show To Be Held In Varanasi In October, PM Modi Likely To Attend
national_raw_news.content: Varanasi Gears Up For Three-Day IAF Air Show Over Ganga, PM Modi Likely To Attend States Three-Day IAF Air Show To Be Held In Varanasi In October, PM Modi Likely To Attend Swarajya Staff Sep 20, 2026 | Updated 12:27 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Three IAF Rafales flying in formation. (Via PIB) Varanasi is set to witness its first-ever air show as the Indian Air Force (IAF) prepares to stage a spectacular three-day aerial display over the sacred Ganges. Scheduled for 22, 23 and 25 October, the event is expected to draw crowds of 20 lakh people to witness fighter jets and helicopters performing above the historic ghats stretching from Namo Ghat to Assi Ghat. The Indian Air Force plans to deploy more than three dozen aircraft for the show, including Rafale fighter jets, the renowned Suryakiran aerobatic team, Rudra helicopters, C-295 aircraft, Tejas fighters and Dakota aircraft. Performances will take place between noon and 2pm each day, with displays lasting approximately 90 minutes as three to five aircraft showcase aerial manoeuvres simultaneously over the river. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to attend as chief guest on the final day, with Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and senior military officials also likely to participate. Air Force authorities have coordinated extensively with Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport officials, with Suryakiran jets taking off from Varanasi Airport whilst other aircraft will fly from surrounding districts. District administration has begun preparations to manage the anticipated crowds, with special arrangements being made across 84 ghats along the riverfront. Namo Ghat, designated as the main control centre, will be handed over to Air Force control from 16 October, with public access restricted during the setup period. Officials have enlisted support from neighbouring Chandauli, Ghazipur and Jaunpur districts to handle crowd management and security. Rehearsals for the historic event will commence on 20 October and continue through 22 October. The Rajghat bridge and boat services on the Ganges will remain closed during performances for safety reasons. Local authorities are preparing for crowds comparable to the Dev Deepavali festival, with arrangements for approximately 5,000 VIP guests from across India and abroad.
